 Newsmax soars after strong interest in the midterm election boosted results
 1 min read NMAX Newsmax NMAX said its third quarter was the strongest in its history as a public company. CEO Christopher Ruddy noted engagement rose through the midterm campaign. 
 Revenue rose 52.5% year over year to $69.0M. The tally included $14.0M recognized in connection with a non-recurring service revenue termination payment of an advertising purchase agreement with a customer. Excluding the one-time revenue item, total revenue was up 21.6% during the quarter. Broadcast revenue was strong, driven by growth in affiliate fee revenue, attributed to new contractual relationships and rate increases that took effect in late 2025 and 2026, and expanded international licensing agreements. 
 Newsmax NMAX reported adjusted EBITDA of $15.2M after seeing a loss as year ago of $4.1M. The company ended the quarter with $137.6M in cash and short-term investments. 
 Looking ahead, Newsmax NMAX maintained its underlying full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $212M to $216M (midpoint $214M), which excludes the $14.0M one-time revenue item recognized in Q3 and represents 13% year-over-year growth at the midpoint of the range. "With a strong balance sheet, no debt, and a disciplined approach to capital allocation, we will continue to invest in content, distribution, and OTT initiatives that support long-term growth and sustainable, long-term shareholder value," noted CFO Darryle BUrnham. 
 Shares of Newsmax NMAX soared 13.3% in postmarket action.
